The Numbers Don't Lie: Is That Tucson Investment Property Really a Good Deal?

A rental listing can look like a winner until the real numbers arrive.

By Reddy Appraisal LLCOctober 22, 20262 min read

IN THIS ARTICLE

Look beyond the advertised rentRun more than one scenarioTest the deal against conservative assumptionsMore in Investment & Business ↗← All 24 articles

THE SHORT ANSWER

The best deals are often the ones that survive conservative assumptions. Review comparable sales, neighborhood demand, property condition, and likely capital expenses before getting emotionally attached.

Look beyond the advertised rent

A rental listing can look like a winner until the real numbers arrive. A promising monthly rent is only the beginning; mortgage payments, taxes, insurance, maintenance, vacancy, management, and future repairs can quickly change the picture. For buyers looking at Tucson duplexes, triplexes, or fourplexes, the smartest offer starts with a realistic budget, not an optimistic rent estimate.

Run more than one scenario

Run more than one scenario before you buy. What happens if the property sits vacant for a month, insurance rises, or the air conditioner needs replacing? Compare actual leases with market rents, and separate gross income from net operating income. Cash flow depends on financing, while market value depends on what informed buyers are willing to pay. A property can appraise well and still be a poor fit for your investment goals.

Test the deal against conservative assumptions

The best deals are often the ones that survive conservative assumptions. Review comparable sales, neighborhood demand, property condition, and likely capital expenses before getting emotionally attached. For one- to four-unit residential investment properties in Southern Arizona, an independent appraisal can add useful perspective to your acquisition or long-term hold strategy.
